candidates.bio:
Toronto singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Charlotte Cornfield developed through Canada's independent music circuit as a writer whose songs make ordinary detail carry unusual emotional weight. Trained as a drummer as well as a songwriter, she moved between percussion work and her own records before albums such as Future Snowbird and The Shape of Your Name sharpened a conversational folk-rock style built around close observation rather than grand gestures. The Shape of Your Name reached the 2019 Polaris Music Prize Long List, giving broader national recognition to a catalogue that had grown steadily through clubs, small labels and collaborations.

Highs in the Minuses, released in 2021, expanded Cornfield's audience and established a looser full-band sound around writing that could be funny, anxious and devastating within the same song. Could Have Done Anything followed in 2023 and drew strong international critical attention while Cornfield toured across North America and Europe with artists including Broken Social Scene, Julien Baker and Bonny Light Horseman. By 2025, Polaris was presenting her as an alum with a distinctive songwriting voice, reflecting how a once-under-the-radar Toronto artist had become an increasingly visible part of Canada's contemporary singer-songwriter landscape.

Her sixth album, Hurts Like Hell, arrived in March 2026 through Next Door Records in Canada and Merge Records internationally. Produced by Philip Weinrobe and made with a full backing band, the record includes contributions from Feist, Buck Meek and members of Palehound and Lake Street Dive. It was Cornfield's first album recorded after becoming a parent, and its wider collaborative approach mirrors a career that has gradually grown outward without sanding away the specificity of her writing. Cornfield matters less as a conventional breakout story than as an example of how sustained independent craft can become its own form of influence and international reach.

Vancouver six-piece Chase the Bear is a Canadian rock band known for high-energy, hook-heavy songs and a hard-driving live show. Signed to Rock Is Dead Records/604 Records, the group released its debut album Honey in 2023 and followed it with new singles and the Demons EP.
Whitby, Ontario project Chastity, led by Brandon Williams, makes emotionally charged Canadian punk, hardcore and shoegaze rooted in suburban isolation and community-building.

Chasé Scanz is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with Vancouver's Indigenous rap scene and the Hereditary Sound circle. His collaborations with Sekawnee and EfrainYB include Nations, Relatives and Get Up and Dance, while his own releases include Fashion District. Northern Dial carries Chasé Scanz as part of its contemporary Indigenous and West Coast Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Vancouver emcee and producer Checkmate became one of the city's key late-1990s hip-hop voices before Canadian rap had reliable national pathways. A mainstay of the local scene, he appeared on the Rascalz' "Clockwork" from Cash Crop and then delivered one of the verses on the 1998 posse cut "Northern Touch." The record joined Vancouver and Toronto artists on one track, won the 1999 JUNO Award for Best Rap Recording and helped turn a regional network into a visible statement about Canadian hip-hop as a national culture.

Checkmate built that exposure into a solo catalogue rather than living off one famous feature. His early single "The Longshot" established a battle-ready presence, while songs such as "These Days And Times," "Would You Die?" and "Respect It" showed a broader writer interested in social pressure, moral conflict and survival as well as lyrical competition. The 2001 album Welcome to the Game pulled those sides together without locking him into one style, and Exclaim! positioned the release as the full-length arrival of a Vancouver MC who had already paid significant local dues.

His career also helps map the continuity of Vancouver rap beyond its best-known early breakthroughs. Checkmate continued working with longtime collaborator Concise as Defenders of the Faith and remained active into the 2020s through releases including "Aviator Game" with DJ Kemo and Ras Kass and the later Pro Game 2 project. That longevity makes him more than the least-famous name on "Northern Touch": he is a durable link between the Rascalz-era Vancouver underground, independent West Coast rap and the artists who kept that scene moving after the national spotlight shifted elsewhere.

CHINO WAWA is a Montréal Afro-pop recording artist whose catalogue blends contemporary pop, R&B and Afro-influenced production. Apple Music identifies Montréal, Quebec, Canada as his origin, and his releases include the GLUE projects alongside collaborations with artists including YessirXD. FLAWS from GLUE ll is his Northern Dial library credit.

Chippewa Travellers is an Anishinaabeg family drum group originally from Neyaashiinigmiing (Cape Croker), Ontario. The group has recorded traditional powwow music and reached wider audiences through collaborations with The Halluci Nation, including Ba Na Na and other releases.
Toronto singer-songwriter Chloë Doucet makes jangly, guitar-driven indie pop that draws on classic pop-rock textures while keeping a contemporary Canadian songwriting sensibility.

Scarborough-born rapper Choclair emerged in the 1990s as one of the artists who helped move Toronto hip-hop from an independent scene toward national visibility. After early releases on his own Kneedeep Records, he became part of the cross-country breakthrough around Rascalz's "Northern Touch," appearing alongside Kardinal Offishall, Thrust and Checkmate on a record that became a defining statement for Canadian rap at the end of the decade.

His 1999 major-label debut Ice Cold turned that momentum into a solo breakthrough. The album went gold quickly in Canada, while the Kardinal Offishall-produced single "Let's Ride" crossed onto Canadian and U.S. rap charts. Ice Cold won the JUNO Award for Best Rap Recording, and Choclair went on to accumulate multiple JUNO and MuchMusic Video Award wins during a period when Canadian hip-hop still faced limited mainstream infrastructure.

Choclair's significance rests not only on his own catalogue but on the network he represented: Toronto artists, producers and crews building a recognizable local rap identity before the city's later global breakthrough. His work with Kardinal Offishall, Saukrates and the Northern Touch generation makes him an essential link in the history of Canadian hip-hop.

Chris Black is a Toronto independent artist whose self-titled catalogue is rooted in the city's hip-hop and contemporary music scene. His releases are documented through a Toronto-based Bandcamp profile, distinguishing this Canadian artist from other performers using the same name. Northern Dial carries Chris Black as part of its Toronto independent catalogue.

Woodbridge, Ontario singer-songwriter Chris LaRocca is a Canadian R&B artist and songwriter whose credits include collaborations with Bryson Tiller, Summer Walker, Kali Uchis and other contemporary artists.

Halifax singer-songwriter and recording artist Chudi Harris is part of Nova Scotia's independent R&B and hip-hop community. His alternative R&B catalogue includes multiple EPs and collaborations, with performances and recordings connecting him to artists including Aquakultre, T. Thomason, Ghettosocks and Tachichi.
Cindy Lee is the experimental pop and songwriting project of Canadian musician Patrick Flegel, formerly of Women, combining lo-fi pop, doo-wop, noise and glam-inflected performance.

Vancouver hip-hop duo Cipher paired producer Clean’s hazy, jazz-leaning production with rapper G2’s lyricism on the underground album 360 Degrees. The mid-1990s project, including the track Peeps, became part of the city’s early independent rap catalogue and was later distributed by Bomb Hip-Hop.
Toronto duo Citizen Kane is a Canadian underground hip-hop group whose late-1990s releases earned back-to-back Juno nominations and documented the city's emerging independent rap scene.
Ottawa rapper, community builder and entrepreneur City Fidelia, born Luigi Fidelia, pairs Canadian hip-hop with a strong focus on independent creative infrastructure and community development.

Born and raised in Toronto’s Weston neighbourhood, Clairmont The Second, born Clairmont II Humphrey, developed as a true multi-hyphenate: rapper, vocalist, producer, composer, engineer, director, editor, filmmaker and photographer. His early self-released mixtapes led into the 2016 album Quest for Milk and Honey, which was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize and established him as an artist whose production and visual language were inseparable from the writing.

The 2017 album Lil Mont from the Ave earned a JUNO nomination for Rap Recording of the Year, while later work including Do You Drive? and It’s Not How It Sounds continued his self-produced, highly authored approach. His song "Grip" was shortlisted for the SOCAN Songwriting Prize in 2020, followed by another shortlist for "Dream" in 2021. He also received the Prism Prize’s Hi-Fidelity Award for his work in music video, reinforcing how central directing and visual storytelling are to his practice.

Clairmont’s influence is especially important within Toronto’s independent hip-hop ecosystem. He represents a model in which an artist does not simply rap over production but controls the wider sonic and visual world around the music. Collaborations and production relationships across Toronto’s alternative R&B and rap scenes have made him a connective figure between neighbourhood-rooted hip-hop, experimental composition and independent filmmaking.

Toronto songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Adam LaFramboise records as Clothesline From Hell, blending acoustic songwriting with hip-hop loops, programmed drums and scrappy alternative-pop production.

Montréal singer-songwriter and pianist Béatrice Martin became Cœur de pirate while still a teenager, breaking through with her self-titled 2008 debut. Built around piano, close-miked vocals and concise French-language pop writing, Cœur de pirate became a major success in both Canada and France, with "Comme des enfants" helping establish Martin as a francophone artist capable of crossing the Atlantic without abandoning Québec's musical identity. The album's success was followed by Blonde, which broadened the arrangements while consolidating her audience in Québec and Europe.

Roses introduced more English-language material and made Martin's bilingual reach explicit, while En cas de tempête, ce jardin sera fermé returned to a more intimate francophone centre. After vocal-cord surgery, she released the instrumental piano album Perséides, then Impossible à aimer, which won the 2022 JUNO for Francophone Album of the Year. Cavale, released in 2025, extended a catalogue that has moved between piano pop, orchestral textures, electronic production and soundtrack work without losing the melodic directness of her debut.

Cœur de pirate matters as one of the most visible modern bridges between Québec pop and the wider francophone world. Martin's career shows that French-language Canadian music can travel internationally on its own terms rather than using English crossover as the only measure of reach. Her later role as president and artistic director of Bravo Musique also moved that influence behind the scenes, giving her a direct hand in supporting another generation of Québec artists.

Cola H., also known as Colanthony Humphrey, is a Toronto multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, producer and artist active across the city's rock, hip-hop and independent music communities. He is also known for his work with The OBGMs and for production and collaborative projects beyond the band. Northern Dial carries Cola H. as part of its Toronto artist and producer catalogue.

Comrade is Calgary producer Evgeniy 'Comrade' Bykovets, one half of the lo-fi soul duo Sargeant X Comrade. His production combines hip-hop sampling, soul, funk and jazz textures behind vocalist Yolanda Sargeant. Northern Dial carries Comrade as part of its Calgary producer and soul catalogue.

Vancouver MC and producer Concise the Black Knight is a longtime figure in the city's hip-hop community. Born in North Africa and raised in Vancouver after immigrating to Canada, he came up alongside Checkmate, appeared in the Northern Touch era and built a solo catalogue rooted in independent West Coast rap.

Connor Newton is a Saskatoon-born Canadian saxophonist, multi-instrumentalist, producer and educator. After studying jazz performance in Edmonton and at the University of Toronto, he returned to Saskatoon and has worked with artists including Bombargo, vbnd, Katie Tupper and Collective Order while also releasing hip-hop-informed solo work as Contrafact. His saxophone performances on vbnd's Name (On My Tongue) and No Other Feeling account for his Northern Dial library credits.
Canadian rapper and songwriter known for concise, high-energy hip-hop releases and short-form music content.
Toronto indie-pop group cootie catcher mixes twee, jangle pop, new wave and lo-fi electronics with playful arrangements and emotionally direct songwriting.

Corey Writez is a Halifax hip-hop artist active in Nova Scotia's independent rap scene. He appears on Aquakultre and DJ Uncle Fester's Halifax-recorded album Bleeding Gums Murphy on the track 'Autographs' and has been billed as a local Halifax act in live-event promotion. Northern Dial carries Corey Writez as part of its Atlantic Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Kitchener rock band Courage My Love built a Canadian pop-punk and alternative-rock following around the twin-sister core of Mercedes and Phoenix Arn-Horn before the project ended in 2020.
Canadian singer-songwriter Craig Smart is a pop and dance vocalist known for solo radio releases and collaborations with electronic producers including Marc Mysterio and Trevor Guthrie.

Crash Test Dummies emerged from Winnipeg with a sound built around Brad Roberts' unusually deep baritone, literate storytelling and arrangements that drew as much from folk and roots music as alternative rock. Their 1991 debut The Ghosts That Haunt Me became a major Canadian breakthrough through "Superman's Song," helping the group win the 1992 JUNO Award for Group of the Year. The song's reflective writing and Roberts' deadpan delivery established an identity that was immediately recognizable before the band had its international hit.

God Shuffled His Feet took that identity worldwide in 1993. "Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm" became a major international single, while the album's mixture of eccentric narratives, acoustic textures and pop arrangements earned the band three Grammy nominations at the 1995 ceremony, including Best New Artist and Best Alternative Music Album. A Worm's Life and Give Yourself a Hand followed, with the latter moving into more electronic production, while Roberts continued the project through later recordings even as its commercial scale changed.

The band's legacy is larger than the novelty sometimes attached to its most famous song. Crash Test Dummies translated a distinctly Winnipeg-rooted, songwriter-driven sensibility into an international alternative-pop moment without disguising Roberts' odd humour or literary instincts. Anniversary tours for both God Shuffled His Feet and The Ghosts That Haunt Me eventually brought the group back to sustained international touring, demonstrating that the catalogue retained an audience decades after its 1990s peak.

Culture is a Canadian-Bahamian rapper and reggae artist best known for appearing on Karl Wolf's hit cover of Africa. His work sits at the intersection of Canadian hip-hop, reggae and pop, with Africa reaching the upper tier of the Canadian Hot 100 and bringing his voice to a national audience. Northern Dial carries Culture as part of its Canadian hip-hop and reggae catalogue.

Cupidon is a Montreal street rapper from the city's Sud-Ouest who has been active in Quebec hip-hop since the early 2010s. His catalogue includes solo releases and collaborations with artists including Lebza Khey and DawaMafia, with a direct writing style rooted in the local rap québécois scene.

Cut The Lights is a Toronto hip-hop group fronted vocally by Rochester, the Toronto rapper also known as Rochester Juice. The group has released tracks including 'Run,' 'Too Bright' and 'Back It Up,' and Rochester has described Cut The Lights as his group while discussing its placements in projects including Across the Spider-Verse, Fortnite and NFL Films. Northern Dial carries Cut The Lights as part of its contemporary Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Cape Breton-born musician, songwriter and producer Cyrus Robertson-Orkish has built a versatile Canadian career spanning alternative rock, progressive music, jazz fusion and experimental pop. After establishing himself in Halifax with Dali Van Gogh and solo work as Cyrus R.O., he later became active in Ottawa through projects including Finely Tuned Elephant, GirlBoyThing and Victor Complex.

Montréal singer-songwriter Béatrice Martin, better known as Cœur de pirate, is a Canadian Francophone pop artist whose piano-led songwriting has made her one of Québec's most recognizable contemporary voices.
Toronto rapper D-Sisive, born Derek Christoff, is known for introspective, autobiographical hip-hop that helped establish him as one of Canada's most acclaimed underground MCs.

Montréal rapper D-Shade is best known as a member of the pioneering trio Shades of Culture alongside Revolution and DJ Storm. Emerging from Montréal's early-1990s hip-hop scene, the group toured nationally and released records including Mindstate while helping establish an independent francophone and anglophone rap culture in the city.

D.O.V, born David Oliveira Vieira, is a Toronto-native underground hip-hop artist, songwriter and executive producer. A co-owner of Hella Treez alongside DJ Chino420, he works in gritty boom-bap and hardcore rap and has collaborated with artists including Ruste Juxx, Termanology, Planet Asia and Killah Priest. His 2025 album D.O.V is GOD includes the Northern Dial tracks Back From The Dead and Fallen Angels.
Toronto production team Da Grassroots helped shape Canadian hip-hop through sample-driven production for artists including Ghetto Concept, Choclair and Saukrates and the album Passage Through Time.

Toronto production trio Da Grassroots, made up of Mr. Attic, Mr. Murray and Swiff, became one of the key behind-the-scenes forces in the city's 1990s hip-hop development. Working together from the turn of the decade, they supplied sample-rich, jazz-informed production for an independent scene that had little major-label support. Their work with Ghetto Concept was especially important: the group's "Certified" and "E-Z on Tha Motion" won consecutive JUNO Awards for Best Rap Recording in 1995 and 1996, helping prove that Toronto's independently released rap could earn national recognition on its own terms.

Da Grassroots also helped build infrastructure around the music. Mr. Attic and Swiff launched B.E. Records and released their own material, while the trio's relationships with artists including Choclair, Saukrates, Thrust, Ghetto Concept and others created a network in which producers were not simply supplying beats but helping define a shared Toronto sound. Their 1999 album Passage Through Time brought that network into one project, pairing the trio's understated production with a broad cross-section of local MCs. Tracks such as "Thematics" and "Postal Work" showed how comfortably their style could move from stripped-down jazz loops to dub and harder rhythmic textures without losing its identity.

That role makes Da Grassroots historically significant even though the group never became a household name. They were part of the connective tissue between the first nationally visible wave of Canadian rap and the deeper independent ecosystem that produced Choclair, Saukrates, Kardinal Offishall and the artists around them. After the group period, its members continued with production and label work, extending that influence beyond a single album. In Toronto hip-hop history, Da Grassroots matter because they helped make a scene sound coherent before the wider industry had decided that scene was commercially important.

Da-P is a Montreal producer and beatmaker associated with the ALAIZ collective and the wider Soulection orbit. His work bridges hip-hop, electronic production and R&B, with collaborations involving artists and producers from Montreal's internationally influential beat scene. Northern Dial carries Da-P as part of Quebec's modern production culture.
Treaty 6-born Plains Cree rapper and activist Dakota Bear uses hip-hop to connect Indigenous storytelling, community leadership and social-justice advocacy.
Langley-born singer Dallas Smith is a Canadian vocalist who moved from fronting the rock band Default into a highly successful contemporary-country solo career.
Ottawa-born, Toronto-based musician Dan Kanter is a Canadian multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, producer and musical director known for extensive work with Justin Bieber and other major artists.

Toronto native Dan Only, born Danny Vee, is a producer, musician and DJ whose hardware-driven electronic music moves through house, techno, breaks and dub. A Juno-nominated artist and one half of Cloudsteppers with Ciel, he has released music through labels including 3024, X-Kalay, Dirt Crew, New Kanada and Hâws.
Georgetown, Ontario-born singer-songwriter Dan Talevski is a Canadian pop artist who first developed an audience online before breaking through with polished romantic pop and dance-pop singles.
Toronto rapper, producer and actor Dan-e-o, born Daniel Faraldo, is a veteran of Canadian hip-hop and a member of the Scarborough collectives Monolith and Perfeck Strangers.
Vernon, British Columbia-born singer-songwriter and pianist Daniel Powter is a Canadian pop artist best known internationally for the 2005 hit Bad Day.

Toronto rapper Daniel Son is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist and Brown Bag Money founder known for rugged lyricism and collaborations with producers and MCs across North American independent rap.
Honduran-Canadian singer, songwriter and producer Daniela Andrade blends intimate vocals, bilingual writing, R&B, jazz and experimental electronic production in an independent catalogue.
Toronto hard-rock trio Danko Jones has built a long-running Canadian and international career around high-energy live shows, heavy riffs and a punk-informed rock sound.
